transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-09-03 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Jared Cole (Stratagem Procurement), Nora Ruiz (Stratagem Security), Liam O'Neill (Stratagem Legal), Maya Thomson (Stratagem DevOps), Evan Brooks (Stratagem Product)

Auto-summary (auto generated, may be rough):
- Procurement/Legal kickoff for vendor onboarding; primary focus on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, SSO (SAML + SCIM) integration, and pricing path for a pilot.
- Action: Redwood to send redlines and pricing, SE to run perf bench, customer to provide security questionnaire answers.

Topics: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA and uptime commitment, pricing model (hosted vs dedicated), SSO/SCIM and RBAC, KMS and encryption at rest, data residency / egress charging, pilot success criteria

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have the procurement and security folks on, so we'll go through the MSA/DPA ask, the pricing path for a pilot and then hand over to Daniel for the VPC/KMS and technicals. Sound good?
[00:18] Jared (Stratagem): Yep that works. We've got about 45 minutes. Our main ask is to get the redlines for legal and a firm idea of pricing for a four week pilot that could scale to prod.
[00:28] Liam (Legal): Yeah and quick heads up — our counsel flagged two DPA items and we need clarity on subprocessor lists for any third-party infra. Also around audit logs retention, minimum retention window.
[00:41] Daniel (Redwood SE): Totally understood. We can provide the subprocessor list, and audit logs are configurable — default is 90 days on hosted, and longer for Dedicated/Private. We can surface retention options in the SSO and console.
[00:55] Nora (Security): When you say Dedicated, are you talking about reserved GPU pools in your cloud infra or do you offer an on-prem package? We have PHI concerns.
[01:09] Sofia: Good question. We offer three modes - Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in our cloud with data isolation), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For PHI we typically recommend Dedicated with customer-side KMS — we can also discuss Private if you need air-gapped.
[01:29] Maya (DevOps): For Dedicated, how does KMS integration work? We need to keep keys in our cloud KMS, not Redwood-managed.
[01:38] Daniel: You can bring your own KMS via a customer-managed key in the supported cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). We do a passthrough for encryption-at-rest keys and support HSM-backed keys via customer config. There's some handshake for rotating keys, we can document.
[01:55] Evan (Product): Does using BYOK change billing or latency? We need to understand cost/latency hit.
[02:03] Daniel: Minimal latency impact for the KMS calls — the main cost is the dedicated capacity and any egress. For BYOK, there is a slightly higher handshake on rotation but token path isn't affected for inference.
[02:18] Jared: Pricing — we want a committed pilot price with an option to convert to a reserved commitment after. What does that look like?
[02:26] Sofia: We typically do a pilot quote (time-boxed) plus an option to convert to a reserved capacity commit with a reduced unit price. I'll attach a pricing worksheet with 3 tiers. For pilot conversions we can pro-rate.
[02:38] Liam: On the MSA side, we need the indemnity and IP sections tightened. Also DPA needs clarity about deletion timelines for logs and training data.
[02:49] Sofia: We'll send a redline version. To be clear on logs — we have separate retention for audit logs vs input retention used for evals. For PHI customers, we can set input retention to zero by default under Dedicated or Private.
[03:04] Nora: Can you put that in the DPA? We need explicit clause stating no retention of customer PII or content unless explicitly allowed.
[03:11] Sofia: Absolutely, we'll include that in the DPA redline.
[03:14] Priya (CSM): Quick note — we also offer an onboarding checklist and compliance pack (SOC 2 report, pen test summary) that I can share.
[03:21] Nora: Yes please send the SOC 2 and the last 12 months pen test summary. Also the subprocessor list as mentioned.
[03:29] Sofia: Noted.
[03:31] Daniel: For networking, VPC peering and Private link are options. If you go Dedicated with VPC peering, there are firewall rules and egress IPs we'll coordinate. We should do a topology diagram during the technical deep-dive.
[03:44] Maya: We need SCIM for provisioning and SAML for SSO plus RBAC syncing with groups. Does Redwood support SCIM?
[03:51] Daniel: Yes — SCIM v2 for user/provisioning and SAML 2.0 SSO are supported. We also have group sync to map to console roles. Minor caveat: SCIM provisioning for external IdPs sometimes needs claim mapping, which we can walk through.
[04:05] Evan: Competitors question — do you support token-level cost visibility? We want per-route cost and token breakdown.
[04:12] Sofia: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns. For Dedicated we push telemetry to a customer-visible dashboard.
[04:20] Jared: On billing — can we have monthly invoicing to our procurement system, and an escalation contact for billing disputes?
[04:27] Sofia: Yes, monthly invoicing is standard. We'll include billing contacts and an escalation path in the contract.
[04:34] Liam: We need to clarify SLA: what is the uptime commitment for Dedicated and what's the remedy if you miss the SLO?
[04:42] Daniel: For Dedicated we offer a 99.9% uptime SLA with credit-based remedies. For Hosted there's tiered SLOs; we'll include exact math in the SLA. If you need a higher SLA for prod, we can discuss enterprise SLA add-ons.
[04:57] Nora: Audit logs — format and access? We need streaming of audit logs into our SIEM or at least S3 export.
[05:05] Daniel: We can push audit events to a customer-owned S3 or to a cloud logging endpoint; alternatively we can enable streaming to your SIEM via a connector. We'll note options in the security pack.
[05:18] Maya: On data residency — we need EU-only processing for some workloads. Is regional isolation available?
[05:26] Sofia: Yes, we have regional routing policies. For Dedicated/Private we can pin workloads to EU regions and provide contractual data residency language.
[05:36] Jared: Back to pricing — what's the pilot billing model? Flat minimum plus usage?
[05:43] Sofia: Often it's a time-limited committed pool with a minimum monthly commit and then per-token overage. We'll propose one with a 4-week pilot minimum and include example numbers in the worksheet.
[05:54] Liam: Legal redlines — we'll send track changes to your MSA and expect a response within 3 business days, is that realistic?
[06:01] Sofia: We aim to respond in 3 business days. For enterprise redlines there might be a short escalation but we'll flag any issues up front.
[06:09] Priya: I'll add the onboarding milestones and an initial success metric: e.g., 99th percentile latency under X ms for a sample prompt set and integration validated with SSO/SCIM.
[06:21] Nora: Performance metric is important. We'll expect the benchmark to include cold-starts and KV-cache warm runs.
[06:28] Daniel: Understood — I'll run bench with cold and warm runs and include p50/p90/p99 latency and token throughput.
[06:35] Evan: Are there any specific limitations around model weights retention? For compliance we need to know if we train on customer data.
[06:44] Sofia: We don't train customer data into shared models unless explicitly contracted; default is no training. We'll add that clause to the DPA.
[06:53] Jared: Who will be our primary contact for escalation?
[06:56] Sofia: For commercial/procurement it's me. For technical escalations it's Daniel. For onboarding Ops it's Priya. We'll include names and emails in the follow-up.
[07:04] Liam: Great. Next steps recap?
[07:07] Sofia: Yeah quick recap: 1) Sofia sends redlined MSA/DPA + pricing worksheet by Friday (2025-09-05). 2) Daniel runs bench and shares results by 2025-09-10. 3) Nora sends security questionnaire and SOC2 docs by Monday (2025-09-07). 4) Schedule VPC/KMS deep-dive for next week.
[07:24] Maya: Also please include a sample network/topology doc for Dedicated. That will help our infra team.
[07:29] Daniel: Will do.
[07:31] Priya: I'll attach onboarding checklist and a proposed timeline template.
[07:34] Sofia: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:37] (brief silence)
[07:40] Jared: No, that's it. We'll review and expect the docs. Thanks everyone.
[07:44] Sofia: Thanks all - follow up from Redwood by Friday.

End-of-meeting recap (auto):
- Documents to be shared: redlined MSA + DPA, pricing worksheet, SOC2 & pen-test summary, subprocessor list, onboarding checklist, topology diagram, benchmark results.
- Pilot: proposed 4-week pilot with option to convert to reserved capacity.
- Security: BYOK/KMS supported, SOC2 available, audit logs export options.
- Next meeting: technical deep-dive on VPC/KMS (TBD, aim for week of 2025-09-08).

Action items (re-stated):
